definition: The intermediate tokens a model emits before its answer, and across 23 sources an object the archive is careful to describe rather than to interpret -- one source proposes 'derivational trace' as a neutral stand-in precisely because reading these tokens as reasoning is unsupported by the available evidence and, it argues, actively harmful. What is established is largely formal and negative. Formally, generating intermediate tokens lifts the expressive ceiling of a bounded-depth transformer, with the number of steps tied to a circuit class; one archived construction realises graph traversal in two layers and a linear-step branching measure without layer normalisation, and another shows a sharpness-based bound growing linearly rather than exponentially in the relevant parameter for a parity family. Empirically the trace and the answer are separate information channels: content present in one can be absent from the other in both directions, traces can be swapped between problems or deleted with the answer unchanged, and post-training that improves accuracy need not improve the trace's semantic validity. The corpus's practical positions are that the trace is useful as a consistency check against the answer rather than as an account of computation, that its length is a compute knob with a bend in the curve, and that a large fraction of it is redundant -- with the caveat from a head-to-head comparison that redundancy is diffuse rather than located in any identifiable class of step.

evidence.note: Bootstraps a model's reasoning ability from a handful of rationale examples by generating rationales, keeping only those that reach the right answer, and finetuning on them in a loop.
evidence.title: STaR: Bootstrapping Reasoning With Reasoning

evidence.note: Generalizes chain-of-thought into a search over a tree of intermediate 'thoughts', letting a model self-evaluate branches, look ahead and backtrack instead of committing to one left-to-right path.
evidence.title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models

evidence.note: Finds that ternary post-training quantization of a reasoning model collapses because the calibration set is web text, and repairs it by calibrating on chain-of-thought traces the target model generates for itself.
evidence.title: Attend to Your Own Thoughts: Breaking the Barrier for Post-Training Quantization of Reasoning LLMs through the Lens of 1.58-Bit Quantization

evidence.note: Reformulates chart question answering as a chain in which every reasoning step carries a predicted image region, trains that pairing through a curriculum graded by nesting depth, and finds explicit intermediate grounding worth 8.78 points over letting the model attend implicitly.
evidence.title: CURV: Enhancing Chart Understanding Through Curriculum Visual Grounded Reasoning

evidence.note: Synthesizes Cognitive Behavioral Therapy dialogues using a CoT strategy grounded in CBT guidelines plus a resistance orchestrator that steers simulated patients away from sycophantic compliance.
evidence.title: ODRA: Synthesizing Cognitive Behavioral Therapy Sessions with Structured Chain-Of-Thought and Dynamic Patient Resistance

evidence.note: An Italian proverb benchmark on which models complete proverbs successfully but fail multiple-choice selection when no correct option is present, with CoT analysis showing they name the right ending while failing to notice its absence.
evidence.title: Easy to Complete, Hard to Choose: Investigating LLM Performance on the ProverbIT Benchmark

evidence.note: A training-free two-stage prompting protocol that extracts a problem's answer-space constraints first and then checks its own intermediate and final results against them, routed on by a regex detector.
evidence.title: Constraint-First Reasoning: A Training-Free Protocol for Exploiting Answer-Space Constraints in Mathematical Problem Solving

evidence.note: A trustworthiness benchmark for reasoning models over truthfulness, safety and efficiency, using training paradigm as an analytical axis, and finding reasoning models more fragile than plain LLMs to reasoning-induced risks.
evidence.title: Red Teaming Large Reasoning Models

evidence.note: Reframes unlearning in reasoning models as an intervention on the CoT itself, having the model generate logically valid counterfactual traces and iteratively preference-tuning toward them.
evidence.title: CiPO: Counterfactual Unlearning for Large Reasoning Models through Iterative Preference Optimization

evidence.note: Identifies a multimodal failure where models see the risky visual cue but let narrative coherence override safety as reasoning proceeds, and defends against it by extracting intent before generation.
evidence.title: Mitigating Safety Context Amnesia in Multimodal Reasoning Models via Intent-Guided Safety Reasoning

evidence.note: Switches to soft-embedding latent reasoning only at low-confidence steps, keeping discrete decoding elsewhere, and pushes the soft embeddings away from the top token to stop them collapsing.
evidence.title: SeLaR: Selective Latent Reasoning in Large Language Models

evidence.note: Reformulates reasoning as a search over thinking strategies, showing sparse reasoning paths exist that are simultaneously more accurate and shorter than standard outputs.
evidence.title: Neural Chain-of-Thought Search: Searching the Optimal Reasoning Path to Enhance Large Language Models

evidence.note: Benchmarks whether reasoning models follow instructions inside their reasoning traces, finding under 25% compliance at best and worse as difficulty rises.
evidence.title: ReasonIF: Large Reasoning Models Fail to Follow Instructions During Reasoning

evidence.note: Derives a non-vacuous PAC-Bayes generalization bound for transformers on boolean functions in terms of Fourier sparsity and degree, and uses it to show chain of thought turns an exponential dependence on reasoning length into a linear one for Parity.
evidence.title: A Sharper Picture of Generalization in Transformers

evidence.note: Defines certaindex, an algorithm-agnostic measure of how much a reasoning algorithm's answer has stopped changing, and builds it into a serving system that reallocates or terminates compute per query — saving up to 50% of tokens in batch inference and tripling online throughput.
evidence.title: Efficiently Scaling LLM Reasoning with Certaindex

evidence.note: Characterizes exactly how much computational power a chain of thought buys as a function of its length, sandwiching the class of languages a decoder recognizes with t(n) decoding steps between two standard complexity classes.
evidence.title: The Expressive Power of Transformers with Chain of Thought

evidence.note: Turns each intermediate step of a reasoning trajectory into a numerical feature vector of distances to the answer choices, projects those into 2D to visualize how trajectories move through answer space, and reuses the same features to build a lightweight verifier for weighted voting.
evidence.title: Landscape of Thoughts: Visualizing the Reasoning Process of Large Language Models

evidence.note: Pins down the VC dimension of transformers as depth times parameters times a logarithm, and shows chain-of-thought learning by teacher forcing costs only logarithmically more as the number of reasoning steps grows.
evidence.title: Tight Sample Complexity of Transformers

evidence.note: Explains why latent chain-of-thought excels at exploration but fails at computation by identifying decisional certainty as the governing variable, formalizing it as the Symbolic Index, and proving that curriculum learning is not merely helpful but necessary for training latent reasoners.
evidence.title: Capabilities and Fundamental Limits of Latent Chain-of-Thought

evidence.note: Replaces uniform test-time compute allocation with a training-free agent that picks reasoning tools, a search strategy and an exploration parameter per problem, using a process reward model both to prune within a trajectory and to select across iterations.
evidence.title: What If We Allocate Test-Time Compute Adaptively?

evidence.note: Proves a tighter no-CoT upper bound of AC^0 for constant-precision transformers, and shows T steps of chain of thought let a constant-depth model compute anything a size-T boolean circuit can.
evidence.title: Chain of Thought Empowers Transformers to Solve Inherently Serial Problems

evidence.note: Proves that reasoning can be moved from emitted tokens into hidden states without losing sample efficiency, using a curriculum that deletes thinking tokens in geometric chunks and so needs only logarithmically many training stages.
evidence.title: Transformers Provably Learn to Internalize Chain-of-Thought

evidence.note: Gives the first optimization guarantee that gradient descent trains constant-depth transformers to solve NC1-complete problems with chain of thought, and shows the algebraic structure of the task decides how far the learned reasoning extrapolates.
evidence.title: Transformers Provably Learn Chain-of-Thought Reasoning with Length Generalization

name: chain of thought
